Quotations & Orders
A quotation is an invitation to treat, not an offer capable of acceptance. No contract is formed until we issue an order acknowledgement.
Quotations are valid for 30 days from issue unless the quotation states otherwise. After that, prices are subject to re-quotation, principally because compound raw material prices move.

Our quoted process is: quotation and feasibility report within 48 hours of receiving a drawing, specification or sample; prototype within 48 to 72 hours of an approved drawing; fitment samples within two weeks; production in three to four weeks as standard, or two weeks on an express basis where we have confirmed capacity.
Lead times are estimates given in good faith, not guarantees, and run from the later of order acceptance, receipt of the approved drawing, and receipt of any advance payment due.

For a new part, series production does not begin until you have approved the first-off sample dimensionally. Orders are placed against our published minimum run, or against the quantity quoted for your part where size or complexity sets the economics.
You may not cancel or reduce an accepted order once tooling has been cut or material has been mixed for it, except with our written agreement and on terms covering costs already incurred.

Delivery & Risk of Loss

Delivery and risk pass according to the Incoterm agreed on the order acknowledgement. We trade on FOB Nhava Sheva as standard, and offer CIF, EXW Nashik and DAP by agreement. Incoterms carry the meaning given in Incoterms® 2020.

Under FOB, risk passes when the goods are loaded at Nhava Sheva; you arrange onward freight and insurance. Under EXW, risk passes on collection from our Nashik plant. Under CIF we cover freight and marine insurance to your named port. Under DAP we deliver to your named place, with import duties and unloading remaining yours.

Export consignments are packed in poly bags and labelled cartons on heat-treated, ISPM-15 marked pallets. Where a market requires pre-shipment inspection — including PVoC for Kenya and Tanzania — we arrange it at quotation stage.

You must inspect goods on arrival and notify us of shortage, damage in transit or visible non-conformity within 14 days of delivery, and of latent non-conformity within the warranty period in section 8.

We are not liable for delay caused by events outside our reasonable control, including shipping-line delay, port congestion, customs action, natural events, or failure of a raw material supplier where an equivalent compound is not available.
